title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: a stratified space X whose strata X_i are indexed by a poset I. Each stratum has an open neighbourhood V_i (tubular or conic, the 'déploiement'). For a flag (chain) d = (i_0 < ... < i_n) one writes V_d = V_{i_0} ∩ ... ∩ V_{i_n}. For a subset Z one writes V^Z = V ∩ Z. X_i^* is a distinguished subspace attached to stratum i, presumably the open star or 'deleted' part. Condition (4), from earlier pages, says that V_d^Z ↪ V_d is a homotopy equivalence (the arrow labelled '(h)') whenever Z ⊃ X^*_{i_n}, where i_n is the top element of d. 'Bandes' J, L are suitable convex subsets (bands) of I. V_J = ∪_{j∈J} V_j, and J < L means every element of J lies below every element of L.

This page continues (105)-(108) from the previous page.
- (109): for arbitrary J, L, the space V^Z_{J,L} = V_J ∩ V_L ∩ Z is the union (filtered colimit) of the V^Z_d. Here d runs over the flags in J∪L that meet both J and L.
- If J < L, every such flag has its top element i_n in L. So if Z ⊃ X^*_L, then Z ⊃ X^*_{i_n}, and each V^Z_d → V_d is a homotopy equivalence by (4).
- (110): passing to the union gives that V^Z_{J,L} ↪ V_{J,L} is a homotopy equivalence. Implicitly this uses that {V_d} is an open cover closed under the relevant intersections (V_d ∩ V_{d'} = V_{d∪d'} or empty), so the union is a homotopy colimit over the flag poset.
- (111): the special case Z = X^*_L gives V^L_J := V_J ∩ X^*_L = V^{X^*_L}_{J,L} ≃ V_{J,L}.
- (112)-(113): for a chain of bands J_0 < J_1 < ... < J_n, define V_{J_0,...,J_n} = V_{J_0} ∩ ... ∩ V_{J_n}. This equals the union of V_{j_0...j_n} over j_k ∈ J_k, which in turn equals the colimit of V_d over flags in J_0 ∪ ... ∪ J_n meeting every J_k.
- A struck-through scribbled computation at the bottom is abandoned.

Purpose: to build a 'nerve' or Čech-type description of the system of neighbourhoods indexed by chains of bands, with homotopy invariance under restriction to the deleted parts X^*. This is the combinatorial backbone for comparing the stratified space with its unfolding, i.e. a homotopy link / holink system.
errors: Passing from objectwise homotopy equivalences V^Z_d → V_d to an equivalence of unions (110) requires a homotopy-colimit / gluing lemma for open covers (e.g. Dugger–Isaksen, Segal). The notes treat this as immediate; it is fine under the implicit hypothesis that the V_d form an open cover stable under the relevant intersections.

The 'pour J et L quelconques' in (109) holds only as a set-theoretic identity. The homotopy statement genuinely needs J < L, so that the top of each flag lies in L. Grothendieck corrects this himself in the inserted rewording.

ideas.what: Writing the intersection of band-neighbourhoods V_J ∩ V_L as a filtered union (colimit) of flag intersections V_d over flags meeting both bands
ideas.modern_name: Čech/nerve description of an open cover indexed by chains of a poset; homotopy colimit over the subdivision of the poset

ideas.what: Homotopy invariance: restricting neighbourhood intersections to the part X^*_L above the top stratum does not change the homotopy type (V_J ∩ X^*_L ≃ V_J ∩ V_L)
ideas.modern_name: Homotopy link / holink equivalence for (homotopically) stratified spaces; deleted tubular neighbourhood ≃ link
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quinn (1988, homotopically stratified sets); Mather/Thom control data; Hughes; Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (unfolding/resolution of stratified spaces)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 mentions the 'déploiement' of stratified spaces without these details

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine bookkeeping of neighbourhood intersections indexed by flags and bands, with a standard homotopy-invariance step. It belongs to Grothendieck's unfolding programme for stratified spaces, whose broad idea is known from the Esquisse and was later developed by Quinn, Hughes and Ayala–Francis–Tanaka. Nothing on this page goes beyond that.
transcription_corrections: First line: 'On aura de même' (written 'de =' as shorthand for 'de même'), not 'de ⇒'.
In (109) the index is likely Drap(J∪L), consistent with (107)-(108) on the previous page.
The 'k(h)' on the vertical arrow is better read as '(h)', i.e. a homotopy equivalence; the '(∼)' over the arrows in (110)-(111) is likewise a homotopy-equivalence mark.
In (110) the target written like 'V_{□,L}' is V_{J,L}.
In (111) the left side is V^L_J (subscript J), defined as V^{X^*_L}_{J,L}.
The page header '45' is Grothendieck's own page number; the archive page is 98.
